text: Adults: limit sodium to less than 2,300 mg per day.
title: 2025 AHA/ACC High Blood Pressure Guideline

text: People with CKD: suggest sodium under 2 g/day (under 5 g salt) (KDIGO Rec 3.3.2.1, grade 2C).
title: KDIGO 2024 Clinical Practice Guideline for Evaluation and Management of CKD

text: CKD is eGFR below 60 ml/min per 1.73 m2 (categories G3a-G5) for more than 3 months.
title: KDIGO 2024 Clinical Practice Guideline for Evaluation and Management of CKD

text: Adequate Intake of potassium, adults 19+: 3,400 mg men, 2,600 mg women (NASEM 2019, via NIH ODS).
title: Potassium: Fact Sheet for Health Professionals

text: DASH at 2,000 kcal/day: grains 6-8, vegetables 4-5, fruits 4-5, low-fat dairy 2-3, lean meat/poultry/fish 6 or less, nuts/seeds/legumes 4-5 per week, fats/oils 2-3, sweets 5 or less per week.
title: Your Guide to Lowering Your Blood Pressure with DASH

text: In CKD with hyperkalemia concern: assess dietary potassium (dietary referral) and consider moderating intake (KDIGO 2024).
title: KDIGO 2024 Clinical Practice Guideline for Evaluation and Management of CKD

text: Adults with or without hypertension: a program of aerobic exercise (at least 150 minutes of moderate physical activity per week) plus resistance exercise (at least 2 days per week) is recommended to prevent or treat elevated BP and hypertension.
title: 2025 AHA/ACC High Blood Pressure Guideline

text: AHA/ACC 2025 Table 12: aerobic exercise 90-150 min/week (65-75% heart rate reserve); dynamic resistance 90-150 min/week (about 6 exercises, 3 sets of 10).
title: 2025 AHA/ACC High Blood Pressure Guideline

text: Optimal goal is no alcohol; if you drink, no more than 1 drink/day for women and 2 drinks/day for men.
title: 2025 AHA/ACC High Blood Pressure Guideline

text: For adults with overweight or obesity, aim for sustained weight loss of at least 5% of body weight.
title: 2025 AHA/ACC High Blood Pressure Guideline

text: At least half of total grains should be whole grains; choose 100% whole grain foods.
title: Dietary Guidelines for Americans 2020-2025

text: Limit saturated fat to less than 10 percent of calories per day.
title: Dietary Guidelines for Americans 2020-2025

text: Protein: acceptable range is 10-35% of calories for adults.
title: Dietary Guidelines for Americans 2020-2025

text: Limit cured foods (bacon, ham); foods packed in brine (pickles, olives, sauerkraut); condiments (mustard, ketchup, barbecue sauce); salty seasonings like soy sauce; and instant or flavored rice, pasta and cereal mixes. Cook without salt and flavor with herbs, spices, lemon or vinegar.
title: Sodium tips (heart-healthy eating)

text: Processed meats (bacon, sausage, hot dogs, deli meat) are high in salt and saturated fat; replacing red and processed meat with poultry, fish, nuts and legumes is linked to lower cardiovascular risk.
title: 2021 AHA Dietary Guidance to Improve Cardiovascular Health

text: Eat at least 2 fish meals per week; fried fish does not give the benefit.
title: 2021 AHA Dietary Guidance to Improve Cardiovascular Health

text: Salt substitutes (such as Lo-Salt) contain a lot of potassium and are not always suitable for people with kidney disease.
title: NHS: eating well with kidney disease

text: Use renal dietitians or accredited nutrition providers to tailor sodium, phosphorus, potassium and protein intake to the person's CKD severity (KDIGO Practice Point 3.3.2).
title: KDIGO 2024 Clinical Practice Guideline for Evaluation and Management of CKD

text: Stress reduction through transcendental meditation may be reasonable as an add-on to lifestyle or medication treatment (class 2b).
title: 2025 AHA/ACC High Blood Pressure Guideline

text: PCOS (2023 international guideline): any diet consistent with general healthy-eating guidelines has benefits, and no one diet composition is better than another (Rec 3.3.1-3.3.2); for activity, adults do 150-300 min/week moderate (or 75-150 vigorous) aerobic activity plus muscle strengthening on two non-consecutive days (Rec 3.4.3).
title: Recommendations from the 2023 International Evidence-based PCOS Guideline (Teede et al.)

text: Adults: 150-300 min/week of moderate-intensity (or 75-150 vigorous) aerobic activity, plus muscle-strengthening on 2 or more days a week; some activity is better than none.
title: Physical Activity Guidelines for Americans, 2nd edition

text: In adults with CKD stages 3-5D, it is reasonable to adjust dietary potassium intake to keep serum potassium in the normal range (KDOQI 2020, Rec 6.4.1, opinion). This is set by blood tests and a renal dietitian, not by a fixed food list.
title: KDOQI Clinical Practice Guideline for Nutrition in CKD: 2020 Update
